scope: Independent adversarial data audit (DA7) of four current-holding dossiers not previously checked by this auditor: GM, LVS, RJF, HBAN. 6-8 load-bearing facts per ticker (27 total) selected for the claims most likely to move the thesis or a kill criterion if wrong: headline quarterly figures, guidance/margin track records, leverage/capital ratios, deal/merger dates and terms, litigation status, and beneficial-ownership/control disclosures. Method: primary sources only -- SEC EDGAR 8-K Ex-99.1 earnings-release exhibits, 10-Q/10-K text (including the 'Combining Balance Sheet/Income Statement Information' supplemental schedules GM files with its earnings releases), and DEF 14A proxy beneficial-ownership tables -- fetched directly from www.sec.gov and cited by accession number below. Each ticker's one-line thesis and first kill criterion were checked for consistency with the filings; results noted in the relevant fact.

facts.claim: "GM's 10-Q ... shows Automotive-only debt of just $15.98bn against Automotive cash + marketable securities of $24.7bn -- i.e., Automotive is net-cash positive by roughly $8.7bn" (used as the central rebuttal to V1's 'excessive' valuation flag and echoed in the thesis paragraph and kill criterion 2)
facts.dossier_location: GM.md §6 (balance-sheet nuance), §7 (valuation reconciliation), §1 (verdict paragraph, 'automotive-net-cash economics'), §9 kill criterion 2
facts.source: GM Q2 2026 8-K Ex-99.1 'Combining Balance Sheet Information' supplemental schedule, accession 0001467858-26-000049, as of June 30, 2026
facts.source_value: Automotive column: Cash and cash equivalents $15,147m; Marketable debt securities $4,503m (Automotive-only cash+securities = $19,650m, not $24,719m). The $24.7bn figure in the dossier is the CONSOLIDATED total (Automotive $15,147m + GM Financial $4,987m cash, and $4,503m + $82m securities = $20,134m + $4,585m = $24,719m) -- it includes GM Financial's own cash, which is matched by GM Financial's own $111.7bn of captive-finance debt, not available to the Automotive segment.
facts.note: Automotive-only debt of $15.98bn (Automotive LT debt $15,465m + combined ST debt $514m) is correctly stated, but Automotive-only cash+securities is $19.65bn, not $24.7bn -- true automotive net cash is approximately $3.67bn, not the ~$8.7bn the dossier states in three places (verdict paragraph, §6, §7 valuation rebuttal) and uses as its central counter-argument to V1's 'excessive' tag. The consolidated figure was mistakenly used in place of the automotive-segment figure GM discloses in the same exhibit.

facts.claim: "Raymond James Bank capital (per company disclosures)... total capital ratio ~22.5-24.3% and Tier 1 leverage ratio ~11.7-12.7% through FY2026 quarters"
facts.dossier_location: RJF.md §6 (earnings quality & balance sheet), feeding kill criterion 3
facts.source: RJF 10-Q, Q3 FY2026, accession 0000720005-26-000070, Regulatory Capital Requirements note (two separate tables: 'RJF' and 'Raymond James Bank')
facts.source_value: RJF (consolidated holding company) table: "Tier 1 leverage ... 11.7% $10,651 [Jun-26] 13.1% $11,156 [Sep-25] ... Total capital 22.5% ..."; Raymond James Bank (the FDIC-insured subsidiary) table, separately: "Tier 1 leverage 8.0% $3,612 [Jun-26] 8.0% $3,434 [Sep-25] ... Total capital 16.4% $3,911 [Jun-26] 15.2% [Sep-25]"
facts.note: The 11.7-12.7% Tier-1-leverage and 22.5-24.3% total-capital figures the dossier attributes to 'Raymond James Bank' are actually RJF's CONSOLIDATED holding-company ratios. Raymond James Bank's own standalone capital ratios are materially lower: total capital 16.4% (Jun-26) / 15.2% (Sep-25), Tier 1 leverage 8.0% (both periods). This directly affects kill criterion 3 ('Raymond James Bank's total capital ratio falls below 15%'): the dossier describes '22.5%+, a large buffer,' when the bank's actual standalone total capital ratio (16.4%, up from 15.2% a year ago) sits only about 1.4-1.2 points above the stated 15% kill threshold -- a much thinner margin of safety than represented.

facts.claim: "Parent-level long-term debt is small (the DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount XBRL tag shows only $0.7-0.95B across the last two quarters)" -- cited as evidence of a conservative funding structure (bull case 2) and underpinning kill criterion 5 ('Parent-level debt rises above $5B... current ~$0.7-0.95B')
facts.dossier_location: RJF.md §6 (balance sheet), §8 bull case (2), §9 kill criterion 5
facts.source: RJF 10-Q, Q3 FY2026, accession 0000720005-26-000070, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Financial Condition and Senior Notes Payable note
facts.source_value: Balance sheet: "Other borrowings 950 700" AND, on the same statement, a separate line "Senior notes payable 3,522 3,520"; Senior Notes Payable note: "At June 30, 2026, we had aggregate outstanding senior notes payable of $3.52 billion"

Actual total parent-level debt (Other borrowings + Senior notes payable) is approximately $4.47bn, not $0.7-0.95B -- more than 4x the stated figure, and materially closer to the $5B kill-criterion 5 threshold than the dossier's 'conservative funding structure' bull-case point represents.

facts.claim: "Huntington ... closed two acquisitions within weeks of each other in early 2026 -- Veritex Holdings (Texas, systems converted mid-January 2026) and Cadence Bank (Texas/South, closed 1 Feb 2026, systems converted mid-June 2026)"
facts.dossier_location: HBAN.md §2 (business description), §3 (durability/bull thesis vs FITB), §8 bull case (1)
facts.source_value: "include the impact from the Cadence acquisition, which was completed on February 1, 2026, and the Veritex acquisition, which was completed on October 20, 2025"
facts.note: The Veritex acquisition closed October 20, 2025 -- roughly 3.5 months before Cadence closed (February 1, 2026) -- not 'within weeks of each other in early 2026' as the dossier's business-description paragraph states. The dossier does correctly cite Veritex's systems-conversion date (mid-January 2026) separately, but conflates that operational milestone with the deal's actual closing date in its framing sentence, overstating how tightly clustered the two acquisitions were. Does not change the (correct) claim that both systems conversions are now complete.
